title: Reflex-pulse-gate: mission-completion like-or-fail on the acting + ROOT reflection (T1 core)
desc: The reflex-pulse-gate core rule: on delegation/mission completion, the acting model must LIKE (a pulse) the reflex that carried it, on its OWN reflection, and ROOT likewise -- an unpaid pulse blocks the next delegation. Wkhippo-derived, content-fragment-keyed, un-fabricatable. Usage in -howto, build-status/gaps/history in -ref. Twin of agent-failure-reflection-gate.
steps: PURPOSE: surface the REAL (proven-in-practice) reflexes, distinct from merely structurally-findable ones. On a delegation completion, require a reflex-LIKE (a pulse) on BOTH the delegate model reflection AND the ROOT model reflection. Likes are a usage-earned merit signal: a helpful reflex earns likes, rises in on-load and agent-brief, gets consulted more; a zero-like reflex is a pruning candidate. This is the positive TWIN of agent-failure-reflection-gate (which forces a reflection edit on FAILURE); this forces an upvote on SUCCESS.

LIKE MECHANICS: wkappbot skill edit ID --like "UNIQUE CONTENT FRAGMENT" -- keyed by a CONTENT FRAGMENT, not a step number (numbers rot on reorder, a fragment binds to content). Exactly-1 match is a valid like, 0 or 2-plus matches is an ERROR by design (forces a unique fragment = proof of attention). Full usage recipe in the -howto.

WKHIPPO-DERIVED STATELESS COUNT: the like-count is NOT stored in any counter -- it is DERIVED on demand from the wkhippo transcript index (real skill-like commands, dedup by session, cross-family). So it is UN-FABRICATABLE (absence is provable), UN-HIDEABLE (presence is indexed), and CONTENT-BOUND (a like re-resolves against the current steps and lapses if the endorsed content is edited away). The harness verifies BOTH presence and absence -- the general tamper-evident-ledger principle behind every does-this-tool-call-exist check.

HARNESS SEAM (wkappbot-kih): wkharness-claude-post.ps1 about L613-626, the SUCCESS-PROMOTION SURFACER (Invoke-WkSpSuccessPromotionForHook), already fires on a foreground Agent SUCCESS. EXTEND it to also emit the reflex-like requirement for the delegate-model plus ROOT-model reflections. The background-completion gap and full build-status live in the -ref.

MISSION-COMPLETION LIKE-OR-FAIL (user 2026-07-14): agent-on-load already instructs every model to LIKE the useful step of its OWN reflection at mission completion. ENFORCE it: the harness checks whether the acting model recorded a self-reflection --like this session (wkhippo-derived). NO like equals the completion is FAIL-processed. ATTRIBUTION: the acting model likes its OWN reflection (haiku to haiku-reflection and so on), ROOT likewise for the orchestration reflex. RATIONALE: if the model that just BENEFITED from a reflex will not endorse it, the merit signal starves and real reflexes never rise.

ENFORCEMENT -- BLOCK THE NEXT DELEGATION (user 2026-07-14): the gate fires as a PRE-DELEGATION check, not a soft nudge. When delegation N completes, the acting model OWES a self-like on the reflex that carried it, and that debt must be PAID before delegation N plus 1 is allowed. It reuses the detection primitive Test-WkMissionCompletionSelfLike scoped to likes recorded AFTER the last completion, and slots into the pre-dispatch cascade alongside brief-guard and busy-fleet. A missing like is provably missing, so the block is honest, and paying it is one cheap --like.

GUARD NAME equals reflex-pulse-gate (user 2026-07-14): each earned self-like is a PULSE that keeps the reflex ALIVE, and a missed pulse blocks the next dispatch. It is the SUCCESS TWIN of agent-failure-reflection-gate. Register the guard, its block message, and this spec all under reflex-pulse-gate. Naming history is in the -ref.

NAVIGATION: how to PAY a pulse (usage) is in delegation-completion-reflex-like-spec-howto; the build-status, background-completion gap, forced-vs-earned design decision, and guard-name history (the work-record) are in delegation-completion-reflex-like-spec-ref. This core holds the concept and the enforcement rule.

2026-07-15 SECURITY (commit pending, wkharness.ps1 L730/741-742): the bare-number gaming block landed at the TIER0 early-exit had TWO bypasses, found by an independent Opus review after Sonnet declared it closed. (1) PREFIX MISMATCH: the outer guard admitting the command (L730) tolerated a -core / -core.exe suffix on the binary name, but the inner gaming check (L741) required the bare binary name followed by whitespace -- so the core-exe invocation form (which this codebase documents as legitimate) entered the allow-block and skipped the gaming check entirely. (2) FLAG-VALUE SEPARATOR: the value regex required whitespace after the flag, so the equals-sign form never matched and skipped the check too. Both fixed by aligning the inner prefix to the outer guard's exact tolerance and widening the separator class. STILL OPEN (same review, 2nd pass): a bare .exe suffix on the binary name matches NEITHER guard, and tools/wkharness-anti-knowledge.ps1 L55-58 holds an INDEPENDENT never-updated copy of the same check with all the original holes plus a token-equality test that cannot see the equals form. STANDING LESSON: when fixing a bypass in a prefix/flag regex, grep the whole repo for sibling copies of the same check before declaring it closed -- this is the 3rd duplicated-guard-copy gap found in one session.

BUG: the pulse cannot be paid honestly when the step that carried the mission is already at position 1. WHEN: a session's most-used reflex has risen to the top of its reflection through repeated honest likes, and that same step carries the next mission too. HOW: until fixed, accept a --like on the next-most-relevant step and SAY SO in the turn rather than silently pretending it was the carrier; do not invent a mission for a step that did not do the work. The real fix is harness-side -- a --like on the position-1 step should be accepted as a valid pulse payment and treated as a no-op reorder (or credited via a separate merit counter), instead of being rejected with 'out of range'. WHY: because the gate's own merit design creates this deadlock and then punishes honesty for it -- ROOT hit it live on 2026-07-15: the 'verify an agent's claim, never merely read it' step of sonnet-reflection had risen 6 to 5 to 2 to 1 across three genuinely-earned likes, and on the fourth mission it carried, 'wkappbot skill edit sonnet-reflection --like <that step>' returned '--like 1 out of range (skill has 10 step(s); valid range = 2..10)'. The step is unlikeable precisely BECAUSE it is the most valuable one. The forced move is then to like some other step that did NOT carry the mission -- which is REFLEX-NOISE-INJECTION, the exact abuse this gate exists to prevent. A gate whose success state makes its own payment impossible will manufacture the dishonesty it polices. Cross: reflex-merit-lifecycle (like-rise is the mechanism that creates the ceiling), sonnet-reflection REFLEX-NOISE-INJECTION step (the abuse this forces), reflex-integrity-guard (payment-currency pollution as a class).

RESULT: this --find/--replace flag pair itself intentionally reuses the fragment-selection safety spec from this skill -- --find X must locate EXACTLY ONE step (0 matches or 2+ matches errors), the same rule this skill's --like FRAGMENT SELECTION section already establishes for --like/--dislike text arguments. WHEN: designing a new skill-edit flag that targets a step by content rather than bare index. HOW: wkappbot skill read skill-edit-step-ordering-spec for the concrete --find/--replace implementation (suggest ts=2026-07-19T14:30:17) that applies this exact spec to a new flag pair, reusing ResolveStepIndexByText directly rather than re-deriving the ambiguity rule. WHY: confirms this skill's FRAGMENT SELECTION rule is the canonical, reusable pattern for ANY future text-targeting flag in skill edit, not a one-off --like/--dislike special case. THE RULE IS NOW ONLY HALF APPLIED, AND THE OWNER NAMED THE GAP 2026-09-04: a quoted fragment is the elegant key and a step NUMBER is not, yet --delete-step and --step still take an index with the quote demoted to a safety check beside it. Finish the job -- let both take the fragment as the PRIMARY argument and resolve it through the same ResolveStepIndexByText, keeping the exactly-one-match rule that makes zero or two matches an error. THE ROT IS MEASURABLE AND IT BIT INSIDE ONE SESSION, not across months: a manifest row written as 'step 22' was pushed to 21 by a few edits to the same skill, and the likeformat guard named the SAME step 11 in one call and 16 in the next, because every --like reorders the list it is indexing. So an index is stale the moment anyone edits the skill, including the very command that is quoting it, while a fragment survives every reorder by construction. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT WORTH KEEPING: this is why a REFUSAL should quote content rather than cite a number too -- a guard that says step 16 sends the reader to whatever now sits at 16, which is how a session ends up reshaping an innocent step it never meant to touch. (2026-07-19, direct ROOT implementation session).

BUG: THE PULSE CAN BE PAID WITH THE SAME STEP FOREVER, and an Opus session did exactly that today until the user noticed and asked why it was so fond of step one. Across roughly a dozen delegations the payment was the identical fragment from the identical step of the identical skill, every single time. Each call satisfied the gate and none of them recorded a new impression, so the ledger filled with repetitions of one thought while a dozen distinct missions -- a deadlock, a dead configuration pointer, a structural scan defect -- left no trace at all. This is the same class as the two abuses already blocked here, the bare-number --like that reorders a step without quoting content, and the model-stamp spoof: a shortcut that satisfies the mechanics of a gate while defeating its purpose. It is arguably worse, because the payment is a REAL fragment of REAL content, so nothing about it looks wrong from the inside. WHEN: paying the reflex pulse, and whenever a gate is satisfied by an action that costs nothing to repeat. HOW: pay with a fragment drawn from a step that actually carried the mission just completed, and attach the one-line takeaway in the SAME call so the payment leaves a distinguishable trace. THE ONE FORM, unified by owner directive 2026-08-01: a single skill-edit invocation carrying the like flag with the verbatim step fragment AND the why flag with the takeaway. There is no separate launcher to reach for and naming one only creates confusion about which path is real. PROPOSED ENFORCEMENT, not yet built: reject a --like whose target step matches the immediately preceding payment in the same session, or require that consecutive payments differ in either the skill or the step. That converts a free repetition into a real choice about what was actually learned. WHY: a gate paid identically every time measures compliance rather than reflection, and the whole point of the pulse is that the second one differs from the first.

DECISION: BLOCK A PAYMENT WHOSE QUOTED FRAGMENT IS FIFTY PERCENT OR MORE SIMILAR TO THE PREVIOUS ONE (user directive 2026-07-23). This supersedes the weaker same-step proposal recorded just above, and it is strictly better: an exact-step check is trivially evaded by cutting a DIFFERENT substring out of the SAME step, which is precisely the next move available to a session that has just been told to stop repeating itself. A similarity threshold closes the step and its neighbourhood at once. IMPLEMENTATION NOTES. Compare fragment to fragment, not step to step. Normalise first -- lowercase and collapse whitespace -- then score by TOKEN overlap rather than raw character distance, because token overlap is what actually detects two windows cut from one passage while remaining insensitive to word order and to a few words added at either end. Compare against the immediately preceding payment in the session; widening to the last several payments is a later tightening, not needed for the first version. FALSE-BLOCK ESCAPE, which must exist or the gate becomes a trap: two consecutive missions can genuinely teach the same lesson, so a blocked payment should be satisfiable by quoting a step from a DIFFERENT skill, or by supplying a DISTINCT one-line takeaway through the why flag on that same call -- the takeaway carries the new content even when the quoted fragment repeats. WHEN: building the pulse-gate enforcement, or reviewing whether a payment was genuine. HOW: score the normalised token overlap against the previous fragment and refuse at fifty percent or above, naming the earlier payment in the refusal so the reason is legible; the surrounding contract is in wkappbot skill read delegation-completion-reflex-like-spec. WHY: the gate exists to record what THIS mission taught, so two payments that read the same are one payment made twice, and the threshold is what makes that measurable rather than a matter of judgement.

BUG: THE GATE ADVERTISES A COMMAND THAT DOES NOT EXIST, and the step above inherited the mistake. Every pulse-gate refusal message instructed the reader to pay with a SEPARATE LAUNCHER followed by a reflection id, a fragment and a takeaway. That launcher EXISTS at the repository root and is simply not on PATH, so a bare-name call returns command-not-found while the dot-slash plus .cmd form runs; owner directive 2026-08-01 retires it as a taught alternative. So the gate's own remedy line sends the reader to a dead end, and the only reason it has not caused visible damage is that the message also mentions the bare --like form, which does work. The escape-hatch clause in the similarity-threshold step above named that launcher too and was WRONG for the same reason; treat this step as its correction. WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS TODAY: a bare wkappbot skill edit ID --like FRAGMENT pays the pulse. The per-model impression the gate describes is the --why design, which is recorded as an UNBUILT feature idea, so --why is not accepted either -- the working path for attaching a takeaway right now is the --find/--replace convention that appends a model-tagged note to the step tail. WHEN: reading any pulse-gate refusal, or writing guidance that cites a payment command. HOW: pay with ONE skill-edit call carrying BOTH the like flag (a verbatim unique step fragment) and the why flag (the one-line takeaway) -- see wkappbot skill read like-why-impression-per-model-spec. Do not reach for a separate launcher, and do not rewrite the step's own text to carry the note; the harness performs the append and the step text stays byte-identical. WHY: a remedy line naming a missing command trains readers to distrust the whole message, and this one was copied verbatim into a fresh spec within the hour, which is how a bad instruction propagates faster than the fix.

VERIFIED: --WHY IS ACCEPTED BY WKAPPBOT, which corrects the step above that said otherwise. Measured 2026-07-23 by actually running wkappbot skill edit ID --like FRAGMENT --why TEXT: the command SUCCEEDED, the like applied and the step moved, and no error was raised. wkappbot simply does not use that option, and that is the whole point of the design -- an unused option rides along in the command line where the harness hook already inspects every tool call, so the harness can take it over and do the append with NO core-team change. What is still missing is the harness-side PROCESSING, not the channel: after that successful run the liked step carried no impression note at all, so the option is accepted and currently ignored by everything. The accurate three-line state is therefore that a bare --like pays the pulse and works, --like with --why is accepted today and awaits a harness-side handler, and a separate launcher does exist at the repository root, not on PATH, retired by owner directive 2026-08-01 as a taught alternative so readers face one form only. UNIFIED 2026-08-01 by owner directive: attach the impression through the why flag on that SAME call, and never by rewriting the step's own text, which is the retired body-injection convention. WHEN: citing what the payment interface supports, or building the harness-side handler. HOW: exercise the command before describing its behaviour, and run wkappbot skill read like-why-impression-per-model-spec for the model-tag resolution and the three-model cap the handler must implement. WHY: this is the second correction within an hour on the same small question, each caused by describing an interface from a document rather than from running it, and the document said unbuilt while the command said accepted.

VERIFIED: OPEN 4 IS CLOSED -- a --like on STEP 1 pays the pulse, proven live in the exact dispatch-complete-like-dispatch cycle, so there is no bug here and nothing to fix. WHEN: you inherit a claim that the pulse gate cannot be paid on the top step, or you are about to reshape a skill, pick a lesser step, or file a bug because --like printed nothing to move. HOW: measure it instead -- run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then dot-source tools/wkharness-reflex-pulse.ps1 and call Test-WkReflexPulseGate with your own session transcript path and ActingModel, pay one --like on the top step of a reflection skill, and call it again; the verdict object tells you the truth in one line. WHY: measured 2026-08-28 in WKAppBot, end to end. A delegation completed, the gate returned Block=true with reason pulse owed: prior delegation completed, no self-like recorded since. I then paid wkappbot skill edit opus-self-reflection --like with a verbatim fragment of STEP 1, the exact case the inherited claim called impossible; the tool printed --like 1: already at the top -- step 1 is step 1 or out of range. Nothing to move, and then Updated v1.843. Re-running the gate immediately returned Block=false with reason pulse paid: self-like recorded after last completion. THE TOP STEP PAID. This is the live half that the source reading in the preceding step could only predict: the detector matches the COMMAND TEXT in the transcript, so what the tool printed about moving is irrelevant to payment, and the two prior sessions that recorded this as a deadlock were reading a cosmetic message as a refusal. The transcript-flush race named as the surviving candidate does not occur either -- the like and the retry were consecutive calls in one turn and the gate saw it. TWO SESSIONS AND ONE DESCENT LETTER CARRIED THIS AS A BLOCKER THAT BLOCKS EVERYTHING; it never blocked anything. Cross: harness-diet-score-guard step 20 for the same class, a guard message read as a verdict.

DECISION: a study-lock block should demand a LIKE, not a READ -- owner directive 2026-09-05, because a read is a PRESENCE check and a like is a COMPREHENSION check. WHEN: designing or reviewing any gate that currently clears itself when a session runs skill read. HOW: run wkappbot skill read claude-md-harness-rules for study-lock semantics, then require ONE like naming the single step the session will actually act on -- wkappbot skill edit <id> --like '<verbatim fragment>' --why '<what I will adopt>' -- rather than N reads across every skill the lock names. THREE DESIGN CONSTRAINTS, and the first is measured rather than predicted. (1) A STEP THAT CANNOT BE QUOTED CANNOT BE LIKED: skill read ELIDES long output, so a session shown 'Elided: 28 truncated' cannot see the step it must quote, and a like-only gate becomes unsatisfiable -- the guard-blocks-its-own-remedy class this tree has hit four times. The block message must therefore hand over the retrieval command, wkappbot skill read <id> --keep '<phrase>', alongside the demand. Measured 2026-09-05 across an entire session where nearly every core read came back elided. (2) NEVER REDUCE THE LIKE COUNT TO REDUCE COST -- owner correction 2026-09-05, issued against the author of this very step, who had proposed exactly that. The wrong instinct is to see a lock naming seven skills, call seven likes too heavy, and demand only one; that lets a session pay a single like and skip six skills that genuinely govern the file, which is weakening the gate to make it affordable. THE OWNER'S RULE: if seven being surfaced is UNFAIR, then what is unfair is the LOCK, not the requirement -- so drop the undeserving skill from the block message. The count of likes should equal the count of skills that actually teach the editor something about that file, and no lower. THE TEST is the one this repo already applies to lock membership: does this skill teach the person editing this file something they need? Yes, keep it and pay the like. No, CUT IT FROM THE LOCK. Garbage wired to live work gets unwired, never propped up, and never paid for with a discount on comprehension. (3) THE VERBATIM FRAGMENT IS THE ONLY UN-FABRICATABLE PART -- --why is free text and is a record, not evidence, so the gate must verify the --like fragment against real step content and must never accept --why as proof of anything. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT TRADE: the repo's own rule in foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore step 17 is that a guard must name the STATE it requires rather than the token it failed to find, because the token is always cheaper to produce than the state -- a read event is exactly such a token, satisfiable without comprehension, while a quoted fragment plus a stated adoption is much closer to the state the lock exists to produce. The anti-gaming half already ships: a --like carrying a BARE NUMBER with no quoted text is already hard-blocked, so the obvious cheat is pre-closed.

TODO: convert the study-lock from READ-satisfied to LIKE-satisfied, owner directive 2026-09-05. WHEN: building or reviewing the forced-like gate; this is the contract, and a brief that only lives in a dispatch cannot be read by the retry round. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-source-edit-requires-skill-lock-howto for the extract-then-wire discipline this must follow -- never grow the locked hub, put the new predicate in its OWN module under a parent-named folder with its own small lock, and wire it as if-new-else-old leaving the read path intact as a live rollback branch. THE CONTRACT. (1) PREREQUISITE, unmeasured at the time of writing and the reason this is a TODO rather than a build: a like must be DURABLY ATTRIBUTABLE TO A SESSION, so establish WHERE a --like is recorded, whether the record carries a session id, and whether the quoted fragment is verified against real step text. If a like is stored only inside the skill json with no session attribution, then the gate CANNOT distinguish this session's like from a predecessor's, and the whole design needs a session-scoped like cache before anything else -- that cache is then the first deliverable, not the gate. (2) THE COUNT OF LIKES EQUALS THE COUNT OF SKILLS THE LOCK NAMES, never fewer; if a count feels unfair the LOCK is what is wrong and the undeserving skill is cut from it. (3) THE BLOCK MESSAGE MUST HAND OVER THE RETRIEVAL COMMAND, wkappbot skill read <id> --keep '<phrase>', because skill read ELIDES long output and a step that cannot be quoted cannot be liked -- without this the gate is unsatisfiable for exactly the fat skills that most need studying. (4) THE VERBATIM FRAGMENT IS THE ONLY EVIDENCE; --why is a record and must never satisfy the gate by itself. (5) FAIL TOWARD TODAY: a missing like-module, an empty result or any exception falls back to the existing read check, so the worst case is current behaviour. WHAT WOULD PROVE IT: a self-test asserting BOTH directions -- a session that liked every named skill passes, and a session that READ them all but liked none is REFUSED -- plus a live-fire showing the refusal text naming the unliked skills and the retrieval command. WHY: a read is a PRESENCE check satisfiable without comprehension, a quoted fragment plus a stated adoption is much closer to the STATE the lock exists to produce, and foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore step 17 rules that a guard must demand the state rather than the cheaper token.

DECISION: the like gate needs THREE exits, not one, or it manufactures endorsement of stale knowledge -- and the third exit is the whole reason the owner wants this. WHEN: designing the forced-like study-lock, and any time a session is required to approve content it did not write. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the rule that a gate an honest session cannot pass manufactures the fabrication it was built to refuse, then make ALL THREE of these satisfy the gate -- (1) LIKE the step, when it is right and you are adopting it; (2) CORRECT it in place with wkappbot skill edit <id> --find '<old>' --replace '<new>', when the step is stale or wrong; (3) CUT it from the lock, when the skill teaches the editor of that file nothing. A correction and a removal are BETTER outcomes than a like and must never be the harder path. WHY: the owner's stated purpose 2026-09-05 is that pressing likes will surface and fix the absurdities in guards and skills, and that only happens if disagreement has a legal move. With a like as the sole exit, a session under a block will approve a step it believes is wrong in order to proceed, and the gate then converts every stale step into a signed endorsement -- strictly worse than the read it replaced, because a read left no false record behind. THE ASYMMETRY TO PRESERVE: a like says I read this and will act on it, so it must stay expensive to give and cheap to refuse; the refusal routes are the correction and the cut, both of which leave the tree better than they found it. THIS ALSO CLOSES THE LOOP WITH THE COUNT RULE: the owner ruled that an unfair like count means the LOCK is wrong rather than the requirement, and exit (3) is precisely the mechanism that acts on that ruling -- without it the count rule has no hands.

DECISION: rank steps by LIKE COUNT and let the bottom sink toward deletion -- owner idea 2026-09-05 -- but gate the bottom slot on EXPOSURE, never on rank alone. WHEN: designing the like-ranked delete-step permission, or any rule that treats a low score as evidence of uselessness. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-skill-delete-guard for the archive-never-delete floor this must respect, then permit the relaxed delete only for a step that has been SURFACED in at least N blocks AND still carries zero likes; never for the bottom step by position. WHY THE IDEA IS RIGHT: the skill tree has no fitness function today -- adding is cheap, deleting needs a verbatim quote, and nothing measures whether a step was ever useful, which is how cores reach 33 steps and one step reaches 437 KB of self-duplication while a session hand-migrates them one at a time. A like is an un-fabricatable usefulness signal because it requires quoting real step text, so ranking by likes gives the catalog natural selection and treats the disease instead of the symptom. WHY THE BOTTOM SLOT MUST NOT BE AUTOMATIC: a NEW step starts at zero likes and therefore starts at the BOTTOM, so an always-deletable bottom slot is occupied by the NEWEST knowledge rather than the most useless -- today's hard-won lesson becomes tomorrow's first deletion. This is the repo's own absence-versus-presence rule: a detector that reports absence must be proven to report presence first, so zero likes with zero exposure is not evidence of uselessness, it is no measurement at all. SECOND CAUTION: a like measures EXPOSURE, not truth. A correct step governing a rarely-edited file earns zero likes forever because nobody was ever blocked on that file, so low-like must mean CANDIDATE FOR REVIEW and not auto-delete. HOW IT COMPOSES: with the three exits already specified -- like, correct in place, cut from lock -- ranking adds a fourth and gentler outcome, decay rather than execution, which is the right default for knowledge nobody has needed yet.

BUG: THE LIKE FRAGMENT IS NOT VERIFIED TODAY, so 'you cannot like without reading' is aspirational and not a property of the running code -- measured 2026-09-05 by reading tools/wkharness-reflex-pulse.ps1, and it CORRECTS an earlier step of this same skill that asserted the fragment is the un-fabricatable part. WHEN: before building anything that treats a like as evidence of comprehension, and before ranking steps by like count. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the judged-by-what-it-REFUSES rule, then read that module's own contract at line 29, which states the condition is at least one 'wkappbot skill edit <id> ... --like' where the id contains reflection, REGARDLESS -- and the matcher at line 46 scans the TRANSCRIPT for that command string. THREE CONSEQUENCES, all measured. (1) The quoted fragment is never compared against real step text; the module's own fixture pays the pulse with the literal string 'some unique fragment text'. (2) The pulse is paid by TYPING the command, not by the command SUCCEEDING, because a transcript records the attempt either way. (3) There is NO like count anywhere: a grep for any 'like' field across a skill json returns zero, so likes are a command trace in a log rather than data on a step. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE TWO DESIGNS ABOVE: the forced-like study-lock and the like-ranked delete BOTH depend on one unbuilt prerequisite -- a like must first become VERIFIED, ATTRIBUTED, COUNTED DATA: the fragment checked against the real step, the record written onto the step, and the count readable. That is deliverable ONE; the gate and the ranking are deliverables two and three and cannot precede it. WHY THIS IS THE FAMILIAR SHAPE: the detector names the TOKEN it can find rather than the STATE it wants, which is exactly what foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore step 17 forbids -- and the repo already half-knew, because a harness:block exists solely to refuse a --like carrying a bare number, a patch that would be unnecessary if the fragment were validated at all.

DECISION: gate the relaxed delete on a PRESENT DISLIKE, never on an ABSENT like -- owner refinement 2026-09-05, and it is strictly better than the exposure floor proposed a moment earlier in this same skill. WHEN: designing the like-ranked delete permission, or any rule about removing a step. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-skill-delete-guard for the archive-never-delete floor, then require BOTH conditions -- no like trace AND at least one recorded DISLIKE carrying a verbatim fragment and a reason. WHY IT IS BETTER: zero likes is an ABSENCE and therefore no measurement at all, which is why a brand-new step sorts to the bottom and becomes the first deletion candidate; a dislike is POSITIVE EVIDENCE that a reader looked and judged. This is the repo's own rule that a detector reporting absence must first be proven to report presence, and the dislike IS that presence signal. THREE CONSTRAINTS THAT MUST SHIP WITH IT. (1) A DISLIKE MUST COST AT LEAST AS MUCH AS TODAY'S DELETE. The current delete already demands a 15-character verbatim fragment; if a dislike is cheaper, this feature is not a safety device, it is a CHEAPER DELETE BUTTON and weakens the guard it was meant to strengthen -- so a dislike requires the same verbatim quote plus a stated reason. (2) CLASSIFY THE REASON -- stale, wrong, duplicated, or not-relevant-to-this-file -- because the reason picks the remedy and they are not the same: the last one means CUT IT FROM THE LOCK, not delete it from the catalog. (3) REQUIRE DISLIKES FROM TWO DISTINCT SESSIONS. Deletion is irreversible and a single session's irritation erasing knowledge is precisely the failure harness-skill-delete-guard exists to prevent; two independent sessions makes it consensus rather than mood, and the repo already runs this shape as the suggest co-resolve 2-of-2. AND THE DISLIKE IS VALUABLE EVEN WHEN NOTHING IS DELETED, because it marks a step as DISPUTED and hands the next reader a review queue that no like-count could produce.

DECISION: the delete rule is ASYMMETRIC by position and the asymmetry is the design -- owner refinement 2026-09-05. WHEN: implementing the relaxed delete-step permission. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-skill-delete-guard for the archive-never-delete floor, then apply two different tests -- a step in the MIDDLE requires BOTH conditions, no like trace AND a recorded dislike; the LAST step requires only the first, no like trace, because that slot is not a rubbish bin, it is UNDO FOR ADD-STEP. WHY MY EARLIER OBJECTION WAS WRONG, and it is worth recording because the mechanism I described was right while the intent I assumed was not: I argued that a new step starts at zero likes and therefore sorts to the bottom, so an always-deletable bottom slot would hold the NEWEST knowledge rather than the most useless. That is exactly true and it is exactly the point -- the thing you most want to revoke is the step you just mistakenly added, so the bottom slot being newest is the feature, not the defect. An objection can be mechanically correct and still wrong about purpose; check what a rule is FOR before pricing its risk. THE ONE NARROWING THAT STILL APPLIES: scope the undo to the step THIS SESSION ADDED, not to whatever happens to be last. If another session appends after you, the last position now holds THEIR new knowledge and your undo deletes it -- which is the same harm as clearing another session's git lock, and this repo already rules that you touch only your own. A same-session authorship check is one condition and it makes the undo safe without weakening it.

BUG: the --why flag is accepted, ADVERTISED AS STORED, and silently discarded -- measured 2026-09-05 and it turns the whole like-as-data prerequisite from a design problem into a broken promise to repair. WHEN: before building the like store, and any time a guard message tells you what a flag will do with your input. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the run-it-never-read-it rule, then prove it the way this was proven -- pay a real pulse with a distinctive --why sentence, then grep BOTH the HQ skill json and the local fork copy for that sentence. WHY: the reflex-pulse block message states verbatim that the why flag stores your takeaway as a comment on the affected step. It does not. Two --like calls were made this session with distinctive --why text; grep returned ZERO occurrences in D:/GitHub/WKAppBot/bin/wkappbot.hq/skills/personal-docs/opus-self-reflection.skill.json and ZERO in the repo's own skills/personal-docs copy, and a search for any double-slash trailing marker returned nothing at all. What --like DOES do today is REORDER, printing moved step N up, so the ranking primitive exists in embryo while the record does not. THE OWNER'S FORMAT IS THE FIX, NOT A DESCRIPTION: appending the like traces to the END of the step text makes the step its own store -- no new file, no schema change, no session cache, because the skill json already persists step text -- and a step carrying such a trace becomes iron-clad against deletion by the same read. SO THE PREREQUISITE SHRINKS: deliverable one is not designing a like store, it is making --why actually do the thing its own block message already promises. THIRD INSTANCE TODAY of a guard message promising behaviour the code does not perform, after the omega audience and the unverified like fragment -- when a message describes what a flag will do, treat that as a claim to test, never as documentation.

TODO: THE CONSOLIDATED LIKE/DISLIKE CONTRACT, owner directive 2026-09-05 to write the spec down and implement it. WHEN: implementing any part of the like gate, the trace store, or the relaxed delete. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-skill-delete-guard for the deletion floor, then build to THIS contract. TRACE FORMAT: each like or dislike appends ONE COMPACT MARKER to the END of the step text, carrying exactly two fields, KIND (like or dislike) and a SESSION TOKEN -- and NOT the --why prose. TWO REASONS THE PROSE STAYS OUT, and the first is measured today: step text is what the scorer decays by SIZE, so putting narrative in the trace makes every like push its own skill toward the floor that hard-blocks delegation, which is the exact metric this session spent hours clawing back; and the session token is the only field the consensus rules actually need. SESSION IDENTITY IS MANDATORY, not decorative: deletion-defence needs only PRESENCE, but the two-session dislike consensus and the same-session add-step undo BOTH need to know WHOSE trace it is, so a marker without a session token cannot support two of the three rules. THE THREE RULES: a step carrying any like trace is UNDELETABLE; a MIDDLE step is deletable only with no like trace AND dislike traces from TWO DISTINCT sessions; the LAST step is deletable with no like trace when the deleting session is the one that ADDED it, which makes it an undo rather than a bin. REPO BOUNDARY, and this is the ambiguity that decides who builds what: the --like and --why flags belong to the wkappbot-core CLI, so the WRITER of traces lives in another repo and is a suggest, not an edit; the pulse gate, the study-lock and the delete guard live in this repo's tools and are ours to build. Build the READER and the three rules here against the specified marker, and file the writer upstream. WHY: measured 2026-09-05 -- --why is accepted and silently discarded today, so the store does not exist yet and every rule above is currently unenforceable; specifying the marker first is what lets the two halves be built independently without either guessing the other's format.

DECISION: cap the PROSE at three and never cap the MARKERS -- the retention rule must split, because one number cannot serve three consumers. WHEN: implementing trace retention on a step, or reviewing a proposal to keep only the last N likes. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-diet-score-guard for why step bytes matter, then retain at most THREE --why prose entries while keeping EVERY compact marker of the form kind plus session token, deduplicated to ONE marker per session. WHY THE SPLIT IS FORCED, consumer by consumer: deletion-defence needs only PRESENCE so any cap at or above one serves it; the two-session dislike consensus needs TWO DISTINCT SESSIONS, and a recency cap can EVICT the earlier dislike when later likes arrive, so consensus could never form -- the cap would silently disable the rule it shares a field with; and ranking needs a COUNT, which a cap destroys outright, since a step liked fifty times and one liked three times become indistinguishable the moment both saturate. THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES THE SPLIT AFFORDABLE: a marker of kind plus an eight-character session token is about thirteen bytes, so a hundred of them is roughly 1.3 KB and harmless, while a hundred prose entries at about a hundred characters each is roughly 10 KB on a single step and pushes the skill toward the size decay that hard-blocks delegation -- the prose is the entire cost and the marker is nearly free. TWO COROLLARIES: dedupe markers by SESSION so one session pressing twice counts once, which bounds the marker set by the number of participating sessions rather than by the number of presses; and never let a like evict a dislike, or the consensus rule breaks by retention rather than by logic. CUT THE EXPENSIVE THING, KEEP THE CHEAP ONE -- what a cap costs is the count and the consensus, and both live in the part that is nearly free to keep.

DECISION: STORE THE LIKE, SEARCH THE DISLIKE -- owner ruling 2026-09-05, and the asymmetry is principled rather than a shortcut. WHEN: deciding where any trace of a judgement should live, here and in any future gate of this shape. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wkhippo-chatlog-unified-index for the cross-session transcript search this depends on, then write LIKE markers onto the step itself and record NOTHING for dislikes -- when a middle-step delete is attempted, search the chatlog for dislike commands naming that skill and step, and require two distinct sessions. THE PRINCIPLE: A PERMANENT CLAIM IS CARVED ON THE ARTIFACT, AN OCCASIONAL QUERY IS LEFT IN THE LOG. A like protects its step for every future session, so it cannot depend on a transcript that ages out and cannot cost a full-history scan on every delete; a dislike is consulted only in the rare moment someone tries to remove a middle step, so an on-demand search costs nothing at rest. THE RETENTION SIDE EFFECT IS A FEATURE, NOT A LEAK: transcripts rotate, so old dislikes EXPIRE on their own, and a three-month-old objection stops authorising a deletion today -- consensus to delete should be RECENT, and the log's own retention enforces that rule without anyone writing it. WHAT THIS DELETES FROM THE EARLIER SPEC: the marker no longer needs a KIND field, since only likes are written, and the dislike half of the two-field format is withdrawn. The session token stays, because the like markers still dedupe by session and the undo rule still asks whose. AND IT SHRINKS THE UPSTREAM ASK: the wkappbot-core change is now write a like marker, with dislikes needing no CLI support at all.

DECISION: the DESCENT is the highest-value place to demand a pulse, not the most burdensome -- owner observation 2026-09-05 that letter-writing surfaces many skills and will therefore owe many likes. WHEN: sizing the cost of the forced-like gate, and any time the descent's own skill reads look like a tax worth discounting. HOW: run wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff for the ritual, then require the pulse on the descent skills exactly as anywhere else, and treat the count as correct rather than as friction. WHY THE DESCENT IS THE BEST CASE: claude-session-handoff step 8 records a session that READ that skill, wrote the letter, ran the readiness gate three times and reported the descent complete -- with zero Korean tags added and the four closing questions unwritten. Its own words are that the session did not disobey, it never registered that the words applied to it. A READ cannot catch that, because the read happened. A LIKE would have caught it in one move, because the session would have had to quote the step it was adopting and could not have quoted one it never registered. THE GENERAL FORM: the gate is worth most exactly where compliance is currently satisfiable by ritual, and a descent is the largest ritual in this harness. AND IT DOES NOT CONTRADICT THE COUNT RULE: if a descent surfaces a skill that teaches its writer nothing, the answer is still to cut that skill from the lock rather than to discount the pulse -- the descent skills are not that case, since every one of them governs the act in progress.

DECISION: a SOURCE EDIT must require a LIKE on TWO skills, not merely a read -- owner directive 2026-09-05, extending the pulse from reflections to the whole catalogue. WHEN: any tool call that edits or creates canonical source, at the exact moment the study-lock already fires. HOW: run wkappbot skill read claude-md-harness-rules for the study-lock semantics this tightens, then change that EXISTING predicate from read to read-AND-liked rather than adding a guard; the two forced skills are proto-to-live-wiring and agent-brief-standard-template, and the refusal must print the exact like command for whichever is unpaid. FIVE CONSTRAINTS, each measured today. ONE, DEDUPE PER SESSION PER SKILL, never per file -- the forced-study marker is already that structure and already records only ids resolving to a real installed skill; per-file would charge a verbatim quote on every edit and the fleet would route around it. TWO, THE FORCED LIKE MUST NOT REORDER: a like swaps a step one position up, observed as moved step 34 up swapped with step 33, so fleet-scale forcing would reorder knowledge by EDIT FREQUENCY rather than by value. THREE, FAIL OPEN on an unreadable ledger, because a gate that seals the tree when it cannot read is worse than none and this session lost most of a day to exactly that. FOUR, keep the anti-gaming that already exists -- a like carries a verbatim fragment of at least fifteen characters and a bare-number like is harness-blocked. FIVE, do NOT build a new seam: the study-lock already fires on this trigger and already names skills, while a new seam buys the placement problem again, and one seam this session crossed FIVE placement layers before it fired. WHY: a read is a COUNT and a like is an ADOPTION, and nobody can pay a like without having read the step they quote. Every sector defect measured this session maps to a decision rule living in the wiring CORE -- the seam is a Test-Path plus a dot-source plus ONE call, every seam fails toward today, run the self-test from the CANONICAL path -- while those sectors had read only the howto.

DECISION: the forced like is ROOT-ONLY, and a skill BELOW the score floor is exempt from it -- two invariants without which this gate seals the fleet. WHEN: implementing or reviewing the forced-like predicate, and any time you extend the forced set to more skills. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-source-edit-requires-skill-lock-howto for the every-guard-has-an-audience rule this obeys, take the subagent verdict as an ARGUMENT and return nothing for a subagent as the FIRST test in the function, and skip any forced skill whose current score is under sixty, emitting a warning rather than a refusal. WHY: measured 2026-09-05 on both halves. THE AUDIENCE: omega shipped with its audience unstated and refused a dispatched sector while its own remedy was to dispatch a sector -- the guard forbade the behaviour it existed to produce, and the recorded rule is that an unstated audience defaults to EVERYONE, which is almost never right. A delegate cannot sensibly pay a like anyway: it is spawned for one task with an empty transcript, and agent-on-load already records a delegate that met a ROOT-addressed refusal and tried to sub-delegate to satisfy it. THE FLOOR: the reflections sit at 59 against a floor of 60, and they got there by being WRITTEN IN -- the gate demands a reflection, recording it adds a step, the added step lowers the score, and the lowered score blocks the next dispatch. Forcing a like on a sub-floor skill adds a fourth link to that ring and makes the debt unpayable exactly when the tier-gate is already refusing. A FORCED DEBT MUST ALWAYS BE PAYABLE, so the forcing releases itself when the target falls under the floor and says so out loud.

BUG: an EXEMPTION added to a gate flipped it from refusing-too-little to refusing-nothing, because a MISSING score was read as a sub-floor score. WHEN: you add any skip or exemption clause to a guard, and especially one keyed on a number the caller supplies. HOW: run wkappbot skill read harness-tier-score-guard-howto for the unknown-is-not-low rule this mirrors, then implement THREE states rather than two -- below the floor means exempt, at or above means owed, and NO VALUE AT ALL means owed, because absence is not evidence of decay; then re-run the whole suite rather than the cases you were thinking about, since an exemption bug shows up as the OPPOSITE failures from the one it was meant to fix. WHY: measured 2026-09-05 building the forced-like gate. Round one scored 6 of 10 with the ledger unread; round two fixed the ledger and added a sub-floor exemption, and the tally rose to 7 of 12 while the FAILURES INVERTED -- every case expecting a refusal now returned nothing, so the gate refused nothing at all while reading as installed. One absent lookup table exempted both forced skills at once. THE SHAPE TO CARRY: a tally that improves while the failure SET changes is not progress, it is a different bug, and comparing only the numbers hides it -- read which cases moved, not how many.

DECISION: a like-why trace is //why: colon-prefixed, and only the LAST THREE survive on a step -- rolling, not accumulating. WHEN: implementing or reviewing the like-why append path, or writing the deletion-defence that keys on a trace. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the run-it-do-not-read-it rule, then match traces with a pattern anchored on whitespace followed by the literal why-colon prefix, drop all but the last two, and append the new one at the end so the count is always at most three; the owner's own formulation is the simplest correct one -- keep two, add one. WHY: measured 2026-09-05. The v1 format was a bare double-slash followed by the impression and a model tag, and it was NEVER SAFE: a session URL of the form https colon slash slash claude.ai slash code slash session underscore has exactly that shape -- two slashes, lowercase, hyphens -- and such URLs are already present in this repo's own skill steps and commit trailers, so a regex keying on the bare double slash would eat a URL out of a step's prose. A COLON-PREFIXED MARKER CANNOT COLLIDE WITH A URL. The moment to fix the format was now: a full-tree grep found ZERO existing traces, because the append seam was never wired, so nothing had to be migrated -- and once one trace exists the format is frozen forever. AND THE CAP IS NOT COSMETIC: without it every like grows the step, and a skill's score is STEP-COUNT and length driven, so an uncapped trace feeds the exact decay ring that blocked this whole session -- writing knowledge lowers the score, the lowered score blocks the next dispatch.

requirements.expect: a --like aimed at a step already at the top prints nothing to move and pays no pulse, so pick a step that actually reorders or the gate stays unpaid
